summary: Lists operational security requirements for the routers and switches of large ISP networks. It defines a framework for profiles, collections of requirements that apply to particular parts of a network, such as the core or the edge.

eli5.summary: A checklist for locking the doors and windows of a big network company, with different lists for different parts of the building.

questions: operational security checklist for isp network infrastructure
what are isp router security requirements
what is out of band management
what does rfc 3871 require of vendors
subtitle: A checklist operators can hand to vendors listing the security features ISP routers and switches must have.

tldr.problem: Operators of large ISP networks need a clear, concise way to tell equipment vendors which security features their routers and switches must provide.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists functional, documentation and assurance requirements for managed infrastructure devices. Each one states the requirement, a justification, examples and warnings, and appendices group them into profiles such as a minimum profile and a Layer 3 network edge profile.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational document, usable as a checklist, as a basis for profiles and for test plans, and it was updated by RFC 8996.

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: Routers and switches of large ISP IP networks

today: RFC 3871 is an Informational document that was updated by RFC 8996. It sets out requirements for vendors and operators rather than a protocol.

sections.title: Goals, Scope and Format
sections.content:
RFC 3871 defines operational security requirements for the infrastructure of large ISP IP networks, meaning routers and switches. It aims to give network operators a way to communicate their security requirements to vendors, and it enumerates features needed to implement policies suggested in RFC 2196.

Out of scope are general purpose hosts that do not transit traffic (name, time, log and AAA servers), unmanaged devices, customer managed devices, small office and home devices, confidentiality and integrity of customer data, and physical security. Examples are written with IPv4 in mind, though most requirements are general enough for IPv6.

The RFC defines a secure network as one that keeps passing legitimate customer traffic, sends traffic only where it should go, stays manageable, lets only authorized users manage it, records all security events, and gives the operator tools to detect and respond to illegitimate traffic.

Requirements use the key words of RFC 2119, and the editor stresses that one size does not fit all: a desired feature in one environment may be a requirement in another. The document is meant as a checklist for evaluating products, a base for profiles, a way to communicate requirements and high-level guidance for test plans.
sections.eli5: Imagine a school giving builders a list for a new building: fire doors, alarms, working locks. This list is for the machines that move internet traffic around.

sections.title: Managing the Device Securely
sections.content:
Management traffic MUST get end-to-end integrity and confidentiality, covering at least configuration, monitoring, backup and restore, logging, time synchronization, authentication and routing. When cryptography is used, there MUST be an option to use algorithms and protocols subject to open review, which SHOULD be the default, and key lengths and algorithms SHOULD be strong and selectable by the operator. The RFC notes that 56-bit DES met open review but is considered too weak. Management functions SHOULD also get higher processing priority than other traffic, so a flood does not leave operators locked out.

In-band management is cheaper but can be saturated or attacked through public interfaces. Out-of-band management uses a separate path. Every device MUST support complete configuration through a console interface that works independently of the forwarding and IP control planes. The RFC recommends RS232 for its simplicity. The console must offer a published way to reset its communication settings, must not need proprietary clients, and SHOULD support fall-back authentication that does not need working IP.

A device MAY have dedicated management interfaces, and then MUST NOT forward traffic between them and other interfaces.

A command line interface (or equivalent) MUST give access to all configuration, support scripting, work over slow links and support a configurable idle timeout. The device MUST allow software installation that depends only on non-writable media, remote configuration backup and restore, and configuration in a simple text format.
sections.eli5: Operators need a way into the router even when everything else is broken, like a spare key under the mat. It must work with a plain old cable, and it must still keep strangers out.

sections.title: Services, Spoofing, Rate Limits and Filters
sections.content:
For the IP stack, the vendor MUST provide a way to list every listening service with its addresses and ports, and the device MUST be able to disable any service, bind services to chosen addresses (such as loopbacks) and choose source addresses for outbound traffic. It MUST offer automatic anti-spoofing for single-homed networks and automatic discarding of bogons and martians, with accurate per-interface counters of what was dropped.

Rate limiting MUST work by protocol (at least IP, ICMP, UDP and TCP), addresses, ports and interface, separately per direction, and on TCP control flag bits. The RFC's example is limiting TCP port 1433 traffic during a worm outbreak.

Filtering MUST be possible on any IP interface, for traffic to and through the device, without significant performance degradation. Actions MUST include permit, reject and drop, filter hits MUST be loggable, and matching can use protocol, address and header fields, inbound and outbound. Filter counters MUST be accurate and able to hold up to 2^32 - 1 values, and SHOULD be able to hold up to 2^64 - 1.

Logging MUST use protocols subject to open review and be sendable to remote servers. Logs SHOULD be written locally to non-volatile storage, MUST be timestamped to within a second or less with a timezone, SHOULD default to UTC, MUST include untranslated IP addresses, and SHOULD exclude passwords.
sections.eli5: A router should be able to show which doors it has open and close any it does not need. It should turn away mail with fake return addresses, slow down a flood from one sender, and write every important event in a dated logbook.

sections.title: Authentication, Authorization and Accounting
sections.content:
The device MUST authenticate all user access, and the mechanisms for interactive access MUST support distinct individual users, with multiple simultaneous connections. It MUST be able to disable all local accounts, support centralized authentication through standard protocols, and let the operator set the order of authentication methods, which SHOULD fail closed if none succeeds. A local method SHOULD exist and MUST NOT depend on anything external.

The device MUST support mechanisms that avoid sending plaintext passwords across networks. The initial configuration MUST NOT contain default passwords, and the operator MUST explicitly configure passwords before use.

Authorization is by privilege levels: it MUST be possible to define arbitrary subsets of functions as privilege levels, with at least three, and assign them to users. The default level SHOULD NOT allow any access to management or configuration, and any change in authorization MUST trigger re-authentication. A recovery mechanism for lost privileged access MUST exist and MUST require physical access to the device.
sections.eli5: Everyone who uses the router should have their own login, no secret passwords should come pre-set, and a beginner badge should open fewer doors than an expert badge. If someone gets locked out, a person has to walk up to the machine to fix it.

sections.title: Documentation, Assurance and Profiles
sections.content:
Beyond features, vendors MUST document how the device behaves. They MUST list every service that may be active with protocols and default ports, the default state of each service and which features turn services on or off. They MUST also document the command line interface with each software release and publish the console's default communication settings. For assurance, vendors SHOULD disclose the origin of the IP stack and of the operating system.

The RFC does not say every requirement applies everywhere. Appendix A defines profiles, concise lists of requirements for a class of device. The Minimum Requirements Profile applies to all devices. The Layer 3 Network Edge Profile builds on it for devices that connect directly to customers or peers, and adds anti-spoofing, bogon and martian discarding, dropped packet counters, the rate limiting requirements and the ability to filter traffic through the device.

The Security Considerations section says that security is the subject of the whole memo, and that each requirement's justification lists the implications of meeting it or not.
sections.eli5: Makers also have to write clear manuals and say what parts they used to build the thing. Then a company can pick the checklist that fits its job, a short one for every router and a longer one for routers at the edge facing customers.
